raw_case_text: A 28 year old female, known to have type I DM presented to the emergency room (ER) with history of backache and lower limb weakness. Contrast MRI of the lumbosacral region demonstrated loss of disc space with paraspinal collection at L3-4 extending into bilateral iliopsoas muscle suggesting tuberculosis. After work up, the patient was started on four anti-tubercular drugs (ATT) regime of HRZE as per the protocol. After initial improvement in clinical and neurological status, the patient returned with relapse of back pain after 5 months of therapy. The repeated radiology demonstrated re-collection of organised pus. The needle aspiration of pus along with Xpert MTB/RIF and liquid culture (MGIT) both showed the presence of MTB resistant to rifampicin. Under USG guidance, a malecot catheter was inserted for drainage of the abscess. Patient was started on modified ATT and planned for surgical intervention and fixation in case of non-improvement or deterioration. After 2 months, the patient presented with high grade fever and discharge from the abscess site for which she was brought to the emergency department. MRI lumbosacral spine revealed infective pathology at L3/L4 segment with associated intra and extra-spinal abscesses causing neural compression in comparison with that of previous scans report (Fig. 1). Suspecting secondary infection, pigtail insertion was done to drain the abscess and cultures were sent for two consecutive days. Aerobic culture of the sample did not show growth of any bacteria and anaerobic culture showed growth of bacteria sensitive to metronidazole. The latter was identified as   Peptoniphilus asaccharolyticus   in both the samples by MALDI-TOF MS. Antibiotic sensitivity was put up by agar dilution method according to CLSI guidelines M11-A8 2012 which was sensitive to clindamycin, cefoxitin, metronidazole, imipenem and piperacillin-tazobactam with MIC breakpoints of 0.25, 4, 0.25, 0.031 and 0.125 (mg/L) respectively. With the culture report, the patient was started on metronidazole I/V 500 mg TDS and the patient's clinical symptoms like discharge of pus and fever drastically improved. Metronidazole was continued for a period of 14 days along with ATT. At the end of 14 days, patient had no signs of active pus discharge and there was complete resolution of fever. Follow up MRI after 14 days also revealed significant reduction in the loculated abscesses in the right iliopsoas muscles while the rest of the findings grossly remained the same (Fig. 2). Patient was discharged with continuation of oral metronidazole for five more weeks along with anti-tubercular drugs and insulin and surgical intervention once the secondary infection settled.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old female presented to the emergency room with back pain and lower extremity weakness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 28-year-old female presented with back pain and lower limb weakness. Contrast MRI demonstrated L3-4 disc space narrowing with paraspinal fluid collections extending into bilateral iliopsoas muscles. She was commenced on HRZE with initial clinical and neurological improvement, but relapsed with recurrent back pain after 5 months. Repeat imaging showed re-collection of organized pus; malecot catheter drainage was performed under USG guidance and modified therapy was initiated. Two months later, she re-presented to the emergency department with high-grade fever and active purulent discharge from the abscess drainage site.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 1 diabetes mellitus; spinal infection treated with HRZE for 5 months, followed by modified therapy after relapse. Denies other chronic illnesses, travel, or animal exposures.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports severe back pain, lower extremity weakness, high-grade fever, and purulent drainage from catheter site; denies bowel or bladder dysfunction, cough, or hemoptysis. Home medications: modified ATT, insulin. Allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile (high grade). Examination of lumbosacral region: active purulent discharge from previous catheter drainage site. Neurological: lower extremity motor weakness with signs of neural compression.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial contrast MRI lumbosacral spine: loss of disc space at L3-4 with paraspinal collection extending into bilateral iliopsoas muscles. Repeat lumbosacral MRI (at 7 months): infective pathology at L3/L4 with intra- and extra-spinal abscesses causing neural compression. USG-guided malecot catheter insertion, followed by pigtail catheter placement. Aerobic abscess culture: no growth. Anaerobic abscess culture: isolated Peptoniphilus asaccharolyticus on two consecutive days identified by MALDI-TOF MS; agar dilution susceptibility (CLSI M11-A8) showed sensitivity to clindamycin (MIC 0.25 mg/L), cefoxitin (MIC 4 mg/L), metronidazole (MIC 0.25 mg/L), imipenem (MIC 0.031 mg/L), and piperacillin-tazobactam (MIC 0.125 mg/L). Follow-up MRI at 14 days: significant reduction in loculated right iliopsoas abscesses.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Relapsed rifampicin-resistant tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott's disease) at L3-L4 with bilateral iliopsoas abscesses and neural compression, complicated by secondary anaerobic superinfection with Peptoniphilus asaccharolyticus.
Confirmation: Needle aspirate pus was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistant to rifampicin by both Xpert MTB/RIF and liquid culture (MGIT). Anaerobic culture of drained pus on two consecutive days grew Peptoniphilus asaccharolyticus confirmed by MALDI-TOF MS.
Differentials ruled out: Aerobic pyogenic bacterial spondylodiscitis (aerobic cultures negative).
Treatment & Outcome: Pigtail catheter abscess drainage; IV metronidazole 500 mg TDS for 14 days combined with modified anti-tubercular therapy. Fever resolved and active purulent discharge ceased completely within 14 days; follow-up MRI showed marked abscess regression. Discharged on oral metronidazole for 5 additional weeks, continuation of modified ATT and insulin, with elective spinal surgical stabilization planned following resolution of infection.
